title: Streamline GPU dependency surface to enable heterogeneous rollforward
creator: Lin Wang
description:
Summary: We need to reduce coupling between the serving runtime and historical CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS APIs that are preventing safe progressive rollforwards across heterogeneous GPU fleets. This ticket is an engineering refactor + dependency cleanup: prune unused Cutlass entry points, collapse duplicated kernel adapters, and introduce a small compatibility shim that isolates legacy ABI expectations. The goal is to make rollforward (upgrade) paths safe across mixed-version nodes and reduce tail-latency caused by heavyweight runtime probe logic.

Background: Over time we accumulated multiple thin wrappers and conditional codepaths to support older Triton/CUDA/CUTLASS combinations. These increase build/test surface, add runtime probe complexity, and induce occasional CI flakes and regression risk during driver upgrades. Recent incidents (see ENG-90123) highlighted failures in kernel selection when a node had a legacy cutlass variant. Rather than ship more ad-hoc guards, we should intentionally prune unused adapters, centralize feature-gating, and add a minimal, well-tested compatibility proxy to limit the blast radius of upgrades.

Scope:
- Inventory runtime usages of Cutlass/Triton entry points and tag callers by required semantic contract.
- Remove or mark dead API adapters that have no active callers in runtime or serving plugins.
- Implement a lightweight compatibility proxy that translates legacy symbol expectations into the new kernel loader API (kept behind a feature flag).
- Replace expensive runtime probe hotpaths with cached capability manifests and a shorter fallback path.
- Add CI matrix rows that exercise mixed-version rollforward scenarios (e.g., driver A with cutlass X -> driver B with cutlass Y).
- Update docs and deploy runbook for operator-facing steps during upgrades.

Out of scope: Full Cutlass refactor or re-implementation; major algorithmic kernel changes. This work focuses on surface reduction and safer deployment paths.

Success criteria: reduced probe latency, fewer upgrade-induced fallbacks, clearer runtime surface for upcoming QUANT loader changes.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory doc listing all runtime callers and justification for removal or retention
Compatibility proxy implemented and gated behind runtime feature-flag
Unit and integration tests covering proxy translation and mixed-version rollforward paths
Benchmark showing >=15% reduction in median probe latency and reduced tail errors in canary
CI matrix includes at least two mixed-version upgrade scenarios and passes consistently
Runbook updated and postmortem template linked for any upgrade regressions
